extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers and legal/technical staff preparing or responding to DOE test-procedure waiver petitions for miscellaneous refrigeration products (MREFs); DOE regulatory staff and stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing petitions for and grants of waivers from the DOE miscellaneous refrigeration products (MREF) test procedure, and the alternate test-procedure requirements imposed by a Decision and Order for a specified basic model (GEA In-Home Grower).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver grant standard (10 CFR 430.27(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE will grant a waiver if it determines that (a) the basic model contains a design characteristic that prevents testing of the basic model according to the prescribed test procedures, or (b) the prescribed test procedures evaluate the basic model in a manner so unrepresentative of its true energy consumption characteristics as to provide materially inaccurate comparative data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE may grant the waiver subject to conditions (including adherence to an alternate test procedure). Petitions should demonstrate either an inability to perform the prescribed tests or that the prescribed tests would yield materially inaccurate/unrepresentative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use DOE-prescribed alternate test procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When DOE grants a waiver it may require the petitioner to test and rate the specified basic model using an alternate test procedure specified in the Decision and Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All representations concerning energy consumption of the specified basic models must be based on testing according to the provisions and restrictions in the alternate test procedure; all other applicable requirements of appendix A and DOE regulations remain applicable unless explicitly modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations must be based on testing and fairly disclose results (42 U.S.C. 6293(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and private labelers may not make representations about the energy use of a covered product for compliance or marketing unless the product has been tested in accordance with the applicable test procedure (or approved alternate) and the representations fairly disclose the test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about energy use for compliance or marketing must reference testing performed under the Decision-and-Order-specified method and must not mislead regarding the test basis or results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to petition for waivers for similar products (10 CFR 430.27(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers currently distributing in the U.S. products employing a technology or characteristic that results in the same need for a waiver must submit a petition for waiver not later than the specified deadline; manufacturers not yet distributing must obtain a waiver before distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and timing are mandatory; manufacturers may also request interim waivers. Failure to timely petition may lead to noncompliance with DOE requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPCA test-procedure design standards (42 U.S.C. 6293(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any DOE test procedure must be reasonably designed to produce test results which reflect energy efficiency, energy use, or estimated annual operating cost of a covered product during a representative average use cycle or period of use, and the procedures must not be unduly burdensome to conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners arguing for alternate tests should show how the alternate better reflects representative use and explain burden issues with the prescribed procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE post-waiver regulatory amendment and waiver termination process (10 CFR 430.27(l),(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: After granting a waiver, DOE will publish a notice of proposed rulemaking to amend its regulations to eliminate the need for the waiver and will publish a final rule as soon as practicable. When DOE amends the test procedure to address issues presented in a waiver, the waiver automatically terminates when the amended test procedure is required to demonstrate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should expect temporary waivers and monitor DOE rulemaking; once the rule is amended the waiver ends and the new procedure must be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of waivers (10 CFR 430.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE grants waivers and interim waivers only for the specific basic models set out in the petition; waivers do not automatically cover future models unless DOE extends the scope or petitioner submits a new/amended petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To cover additional basic models, petitioners must either submit a new or amended petition or request extension consistent with §430.27(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionality and rescission of waivers (10 CFR 430.27(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE issues waivers on the condition that the statements, representations, and information provided by the petitioner are valid. Modifications to controls or configurations that change the basis of the waiver render the waiver invalid for that basic model; DOE may rescind or modify a waiver if the factual basis is incorrect or results are unrepresentative. Petitioners may request rescission or modification for errors or other appropriate reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate factual support for petitions; notify DOE of changes and seek new petitions if products are modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE MREF test procedure purpose and simulation of use
rubrics_metrics.description: The MREF test procedure (10 CFR part 430, subpart B, appendix A) is designed to simulate typical room conditions and user-related loads (e.g., simulates door openings by testing at 90 °F ambient without door openings), directly measures energy consumed during steady-state operation and defrosts, and incorporates correction factors to account for differences in user-related thermal loads among product types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how a product's real-world operating profile aligns or diverges from the assumptions in appendix A when arguing for or against applicability of the standard test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to post petitions and solicit public comment (10 CFR 430.27(e)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE posts petitions for waiver on its website and publishes notifications in the Federal Register soliciting comments from interested parties on all aspects of the petition and specified alternate test procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect public docketing; respond to comments in the docket; an absence of public comment may be noted by DOE but does not by itself determine outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with other agencies for waiver evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE will consult with other relevant agencies (the Decision notes consultation with Federal Trade Commission staff) when considering petitions for waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should be prepared for interagency review and consider FTC-like marketing/representation implications when formulating petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer certification and DOE enforcement use of test procedures (42 U.S.C. 6295(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers must use DOE test procedures (or an authorized alternate) as the basis for certifying that their products comply with applicable energy conservation standards; DOE uses these test procedures to determine compliance for enforcement purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing used for certification must follow the applicable (or granted alternate) procedure exactly because DOE enforcement relies on the same methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate test requirement: no compartment temperature measurements for rotating assembly (modified 5.1(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a compartment with an internal rotating assembly, section 5.5.6 of HRF-1-2019 (Temperature Measurement) is not applicable and no compartment temperature measurements are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE accepted elimination of compartment temperature measurements where rotation would make thermocouple wiring impractical or overly burdensome; provide technical rationale showing measurement impracticability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate test requirement: fill nutrient water tanks at ambient temperature prior to stabilization (new 5.1(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-home plant grower products with nutrient water tank(s), fill the tank(s) to maximum fill levels with water at 72 °F ±5 °F prior to the start of the stabilization period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies initial water/nutrient condition to reflect normal operation for products that supply water/nutrients as part of normal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate test requirement: ambient temperature during stabilization and test (new 5.1(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-home plant grower products, the ambient temperature shall be 72 °F ±1 °F during the stabilization and test periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overrides the usual 90 °F ambient condition in appendix A for this product type; the petitioner must justify that 72 °F better represents typical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate test conduct: use default temperature settings via product instructions or control application (new 5.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a compartment with an internal rotating assembly, testing shall be conducted using default temperature settings as described in product installation instructions or in a product control application on a connected device, in lieu of the temperature settings specified in Table 1; only a first test using the default setting is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows operation via factory/default settings (including control app) rather than forcing standardized setpoints; petitioners should document default settings and how they represent typical consumer use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate test conduct: stabilization and test period for non-defrost plant grower products (new 5.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-home plant grower products without defrost, the test period shall be a 24-hour period following an 8-hour stabilization period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces compressor-cycle-based stabilization/test periods in appendix A with rotation-based timing (8-hour stabilization = duration of one rotation; 24-hour test = one full rotation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate test-cycle energy calculation (new 5.3(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For plant grower products tested using the test period defined in 5.2(d), the test cycle energy shall be calculated as: E = (EP * 1440) / T , where E = total per-cycle energy consumption in kWh/day; 1440 = conversion factor to adjust to a 24-hour average use cycle in minutes per day; EP = energy expended in kWh during the test; T = test period duration in minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to convert measured test energy over the T-minute test to a per-day energy metric compatible with DOE reporting and comparisons.
